# Plain-English Guide: 10,000 What-If Futures (Monte Carlo Simulation)

> **Executive Summary:** Rather than betting your AI budget on a single optimistic spreadsheet number, **Monte Carlo Simulation** tests your business plan **10,000 times** with realistic ups and downs to give the Board an honest **Cautious (`P10`)**, **Typical (`P50`)**, and **Best-Case (`P90`)** range.

---

## 1. Everyday Analogy: Driving Across the State

Imagine you are driving across the state for an important dinner and someone asks: *"What time will you get here?"*

If you give **one optimistic number**—like *"6:00 PM sharp, assuming zero traffic, green lights, and clear skies"*—you will almost certainly be late. Instead, what if your GPS ran **10,000 practice drives** on a computer, testing realistic combinations of rain, roadwork, and rush-hour delays?

| Forecast Case | What It Means on the Road | What It Means for Your AI Budget |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cautious Case (`P10`)** | 9 out of 10 trips arrive before **7:15 PM** | Your downside-protected floor (90% of simulated futures do better) |
| **Typical Case (`P50`)** | Half of trips arrive by **6:30 PM** | Your realistic middle outcome for base-case financial planning |
| **Best Case (`P90`)** | Top 1 out of 10 trips arrive by **6:05 PM** | Your upside potential when adoption is fast and cleanup work stays low |

---

## 2. Why Single-Number AI Pitch Decks Mislead Boards

Most AI proposals multiply three rosy guesses together:
1. *"Everyone will use the tool on Day 1..."*
2. *"...it will save 30% of their week..."*
3. *"...and every saved minute turns straight into profit."*

In real companies, four everyday realities get in the way:
- [x] **Gradual Adoption & Early Learning Dip:** Teams adopt tools step by step. In the first few months, people actually work a bit slower while learning new habits.
- [x] **Cleanup & Fact-Checking Time:** AI drafts emails, code, and reports quickly, but employees still have to check the facts and fix mistakes.
- [x] **Turning Saved Time into Real Money:** Saving someone 20 minutes a day only helps the bottom line if managers turn those saved hours into more finished work, faster customer replies, or lower outside contractor bills.
- [ ] **Unchecked Usage Bill Creep:** Without budget guardrails, monthly cloud bills can climb each quarter.

---

## 3. How the Model Calculates Each Trial

```text
Monthly Net Cash = (Active Staff × Raw Time Saved - Cleanup Time) × Profit Conversion
                   - (IT Setup + Training + Monthly Software & Usage Bills)
```

---

## 4. How Every Dollar Flows (Visual Map)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Rollout Speed & Training"] --> B["Staff Using AI Daily"]
    B --> C["Raw Time Saved"]
    C --> D["Subtract Cleanup & Fact-Checking"]
    D --> E["Turn Saved Hours into Real Profit"]
    F["Setup, Training & Software Bills"] --> G["3-Year Net Cash Range (P10 / P50 / P90)"]
    E --> G
    style A fill:#2563eb,stroke:#1d4ed8,color:#ffffff
    style B fill:#0284c7,stroke:#0369a1,color:#ffffff
    style C fill:#0d9488,stroke:#0f766e,color:#ffffff
    style D fill:#d97706,stroke:#b45309,color:#ffffff
    style E fill:#059669,stroke:#047857,color:#ffffff
    style F fill:#dc2626,stroke:#b91c1c,color:#ffffff
    style G fill:#7c3aed,stroke:#6d28d9,color:#ffffff
```

---

## 5. What This Means for Your Board Decision

When a vendor pitches a single return number—such as *"200% return in year one"*—they are usually showing you the best-case scenario where everything goes right on the first try. In reality, your company faces normal business friction: some teams need extra coaching, early drafts require careful fact-checking, and IT integration takes a few months.

Testing **10,000 What-If Futures** protects you from unpleasant budget surprises. Instead of hoping for the best, you can approve funding knowing that even in a **Cautious (`P10`)** year, your downside is protected—and if adoption goes smoothly, your **Typical (`P50`)** and **Best-Case (`P90`)** upside is clearly mapped out.

---

## 6. Quick Glossary (Under 60 Words Each)

- **Cautious (`P10`) / Typical (`P50`) / Best Case (`P90`):** Out of 10,000 simulated futures, `P10` is the cautious floor that 90% of futures beat, `P50` is the middle outcome, and `P90` is the top 10% upside.
- **Net Profit Today (`NPV`):** Total 3-year profit minus all setup, training, and software bills, adjusted so future dollars are worth slightly less than dollars today.
- **Source File:** [`MonteCarloModel.jl`](src/simulations/monte-carlo/MonteCarloModel.jl)

# Plain-English Guide: Team Behavior Simulation (Agent-Based Modeling)

> **Executive Summary:** People do not adopt new tools because of an executive memo—they adopt when a trusted coworker shows them a time-saving trick, and they quit if the tool keeps making frustrating mistakes.

---

## 1. What Is It in Plain English?

Think about how a new restaurant or phone app becomes popular. People try it when the person sitting next to them says, *"You have to see how much time this just saved me."*

In a **Team Behavior Simulation (Agent-Based Modeling)**, we do not treat your company as one giant spreadsheet line. Instead, we create **325 individual virtual employees** inside the computer—each with their own department, daily habits, and close coworkers.

---

## 2. The 5 Everyday Employee Habit Stages

| Stage | Employee Mindset | Monthly Impact on the Business |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Waiting & Watching** | Hasn't tried the tool yet; watching teammates first | `$0` license cost, `0` hours saved |
| **2. Learning the Ropes** | Trying AI out; working slightly slower during the early learning dip | Pays monthly seat fee; needs coaching to avoid frustration |
| **3. Confident Daily User** | Uses AI every day, checks facts carefully, and saves real time | Generates steady monthly time savings and net profit |
| **4. AI Champion** | Power user (`1.28x` speed gain) who coaches nearby coworkers | Helps *Learning* teammates succeed twice as fast |
| **5. Frustrated Quitter** | Gave up after too many bad AI drafts; seat becomes **Shelfware** | Company still pays for unused licenses until re-coached |

---

## 3. Three Practical Takeaways for Leaders

1. **Word-of-Mouth Spreads Faster Than Mandates:** Skeptical employees start trying AI when their immediate teammates use it successfully.
2. **AI Champions Are the Spark:** Training a small group of enthusiastic **AI Champions** (even `5%` to `8%` of each team) gives coworkers someone to ask for help, cutting early frustration in half.
3. **The "Shelfware" Trap:** If leaders hand out AI licenses to everyone on Day 1 without coaching (*Fast All-At-Once Push*), employees run into AI mistakes, get frustrated fixing bad drafts, and quietly stop using the tool—while the company keeps paying their monthly subscription fee!

```text
Waiting & Watching ──(Coworker Tip)──► Learning the Ropes ──(Champion Coaching)──► Confident Daily User ──► AI Champion
                                               │
                                    (Unchecked AI Mistakes)
                                               ▼
                                  Frustrated Quitter (Shelfware)
```

---

## 4. How Habits Spread Across Your Teams

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S["1. Waiting & Watching"] -->|"Trusted Coworker Tip"| L["2. Learning the Ropes"]
    L -->|"AI Champion Coaching"| C["3. Confident Daily User"]
    C -->|"Masters Playbooks"| CH["4. AI Champion Coach"]
    L -->|"Too Many Bad Drafts"| Q["5. Frustrated Quitter (Shelfware)"]
    Q -.->|"Re-Coached by Champion"| L
    style S fill:#475569,stroke:#334155,color:#ffffff
    style L fill:#d97706,stroke:#b45309,color:#ffffff
    style C fill:#2563eb,stroke:#1d4ed8,color:#ffffff
    style CH fill:#059669,stroke:#047857,color:#ffffff
    style Q fill:#dc2626,stroke:#b91c1c,color:#ffffff
```

---

## 5. Why People—Not Software—Decide Your Return

Buying 325 software licenses does not guarantee 325 daily users. In most companies, an all-staff announcement creates a brief spike of curiosity, followed by quiet drop-off if employees hit frustrating errors in their first week. Once someone gives up, their license becomes **Shelfware**—a monthly bill that delivers zero value.

The smartest way to protect your investment is to invest in people first. Training a small group of **AI Champions** inside each department gives hesitant coworkers a friendly desk neighbor to ask for help. That simple human support network turns early frustration into lasting daily habits.

- **Source File:** [`AgentBasedModel.jl`](src/simulations/agent-based/AgentBasedModel.jl)

# Plain-English Guide: Long-Term Flywheels & Brakes (System Dynamics)

> **Executive Summary:** Over a 3-year horizon, your AI return is a tug-of-war between **Growth Flywheels** (shared playbooks and growing company know-how) and **Hidden Brakes** (sloppy cleanup backlogs and climbing monthly usage bills).

---

## 1. Everyday Analogy: Pushing a Snowball

Imagine pushing a snowball down a hill:
- As it rolls, it picks up more snow and builds momentum (**a Growth Flywheel**).
- At the same time, rough patches of grass and uphill slopes slow it down (**Hidden Brakes**).

**System Dynamics** tracks how these four big-picture forces interact month after month over 36 months.

---

## 2. The 2 Growth Flywheels vs. 2 Hidden Brakes

| Force | Type | How the Chain Reaction Works | 3-Year Impact |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Flywheel 1: Shared Tips** | `Growth Flywheel (+)` | More Active Users → Better Shared Templates → Easier for Next Wave | Speeds up adoption once `~25%` of staff are onboard |
| **Flywheel 2: Company Know-How** | `Growth Flywheel (+)` | Daily Practice + Training → Better Playbooks → Higher Speed & Fewer Errors | Multiplies output per person in Years 2 & 3 |
| **Brake 1: Cleanup Backlog** | `Hidden Brake (-)` | Rushed AI Output → Unchecked Mistakes Pile Up → Extra Time Fixing Bugs | Eats away saved hours if quality rules are weak |
| **Brake 2: Usage Bill Creep** | `Hidden Brake (-)` | Automated Background Tasks → More Cloud Calls per Seat → Rising Bills | Doubles or triples per-seat usage bills without guardrails |

---

## 3. How Reinvestment & Guardrails Tip the Balance

- [x] **Reinvest a Slice of Early Savings:** Putting `20%–35%` of early gains into role-specific playbooks keeps **Flywheel 2** spinning faster than **Brake 1**.
- [x] **Set Automated Budget Guardrails:** Caching common questions and routing simple tasks to smaller AI models keeps **Brake 2 (Usage Bill Creep)** under control.

```text
[Active Staff] ──(+)──► [Company Know-How Flywheel] ──(+)──► [Higher Net Savings]
      │
      └──(+)──► [Rushed Unchecked Work] ──(-)──► [Cleanup Backlog Brake]
```

---

## 4. The 3-Year Tug-of-War (Visual Map)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Active Staff Using AI"] -->|"Reinvest in Training (+)"| F["Growth Flywheel: Company Know-How"]
    F -->|"Faster, Cleaner Work"| V["Higher 3-Year Net Profit"]
    A -->|"Rushed, Unchecked Output (-)"| B1["Hidden Brake 1: Cleanup Backlog"]
    A -->|"Automated Background Tasks (-)"| B2["Hidden Brake 2: Rising Usage Bills"]
    B1 -->|"Slows Teams Down"| V
    B2 -->|"Eats Into Budget"| V
    style A fill:#2563eb,stroke:#1d4ed8,color:#ffffff
    style F fill:#059669,stroke:#047857,color:#ffffff
    style B1 fill:#dc2626,stroke:#b91c1c,color:#ffffff
    style B2 fill:#d97706,stroke:#b45309,color:#ffffff
    style V fill:#7c3aed,stroke:#6d28d9,color:#ffffff
```

---

## 5. Why Year 2 and Year 3 Look Very Different From Month 1

Many executive business cases assume that once a tool is rolled out, monthly savings stay flat forever. In practice, two opposing forces reshape your results over three years. If you reinvest a modest slice of early time savings into shared playbooks and team coaching, your organization builds lasting **Company Know-How** that compounds every quarter.

On the other hand, if teams rush ahead without quality checks or budget guardrails, sloppy outputs pile up into a **Cleanup Backlog** and automated background tasks quietly double or triple monthly cloud bills. Strong governance keeps the flywheel winning.

- **Source File:** [`SystemDynamicsModel.jl`](src/simulations/system-dynamics/SystemDynamicsModel.jl)

# Plain-English Guide: Workflow Waiting Lines (Discrete Event Simulation)

> **Executive Summary:** Speeding up first drafts by 40% will not speed up customer delivery if all those extra drafts get stuck waiting in line for **Final Human Review & Sign-Off**.

---

## 1. Everyday Analogy: The Airport Security Line

Picture an airport security checkpoint with three steps:
1. **Step 1 (Automated Triage):** A kiosk scans your boarding pass.
2. **Step 2 (First Draft / Execution):** You put your bag through the X-ray scanner.
3. **Step 3 (Final Human Review):** If anything looks unusual, an officer inspects your bag by hand.

Now suppose the airport buys a faster X-ray machine that speeds up **Step 2 by 40%**, *and* triggers a few more bag checks—without adding any extra officers at **Step 3**. What happens? **The final inspection line backs up, and travelers still miss their flights!**

---

## 2. How Work Flows Through Your 4 Departments

| Department | Everyday Work Item | Normal Turnaround | Where Waiting Lines Form |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Software Engineering** | Code Changes & Pull Requests | `~11–14 hrs` | Senior engineers reviewing AI-written code |
| **Customer Support** | Complex Escalation Tickets | `~2–3 hrs` | Team leads checking tricky customer replies |
| **Sales & Marketing** | Custom Deal Proposals & RFPs | `~8–10 hrs` | Pricing & compliance sign-off on proposals |
| **Legal & Finance** | Contract Redlines & Audits | `~10–13 hrs` | Senior counsel verifying legal clauses |

---

## 3. The 85% Busyness Danger Line

In waiting-line math, once the senior staff who review and approve work are busy more than **85% of the workday**, waiting lines grow dramatically:

```text
Reviewer Busyness:   50% ────► 70% ────► 85% (Danger Line!) ────► 95% (Multi-Day Backup!)
Wait Line Length:    Short     Moderate   Steep Climb             Severe Bottleneck
```

---

## 4. Where Everyday Work Gets Stuck (Visual Map)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    I["Incoming Work (Tickets, Code, Contracts)"] --> D["Step 1: AI-Assisted First Draft"]
    D -->|"40% Faster Drafts"| Q{"Step 2: Final Human Review"}
    Q -->|"Reviewer Busyness < 85%"| O["Fast On-Time Delivery (High SLA)"]
    Q -->|"Reviewer Busyness > 85%"| W["Long Waiting Line & Missed Deadlines"]
    style I fill:#475569,stroke:#334155,color:#ffffff
    style D fill:#2563eb,stroke:#1d4ed8,color:#ffffff
    style Q fill:#d97706,stroke:#b45309,color:#ffffff
    style O fill:#059669,stroke:#047857,color:#ffffff
    style W fill:#dc2626,stroke:#b91c1c,color:#ffffff
```

---

## 5. Why Faster Drafts Alone Don't Equal Faster Delivery

Executives are often surprised when a team using AI writes proposals, code, or customer replies much faster—yet customers still wait just as long for the final result. The reason is simple: **a chain is only as fast as its slowest checkpoint.**

When AI floods senior reviewers with extra drafts, those reviewers quickly cross the **85% busyness danger line** and a waiting line forms. By shifting just **5% to 7%** of the time saved on drafting into extra final-review capacity, you clear the traffic jam, protect on-time delivery, and turn drafting speed into real business results.

- **How Smart Leaders Fix the Bottleneck:** In [`DiscreteEventModel.jl`](src/simulations/discrete-event/DiscreteEventModel.jl), our *Step-by-Step Phased Rollout* and *Full Workflow Redesign* plans shift **5% to 7% of saved drafting time into final quality review**, keeping waiting lines short and cutting total turnaround time by `25%` to `30%`.

# Plain-English Guide: Pilot Scorecard Updater (Bayesian Networks)

> **Executive Summary:** Wise Boards never write a blank check on Day 1. They fund a **6-month pilot**, check three simple pilot signals (Usage, Cleanup Rate, and Budget Control), and update their 3-year profit odds before releasing next-stage funding.

---

## 1. Everyday Analogy: How a Doctor Updates a Diagnosis

Think about how a family doctor works:
- Before running any tests, the doctor starts with a reasonable **Day-1 Starting Estimate (`Prior`)** based on your age and symptoms.
- Once your **lab test results** come back, the doctor updates the diagnosis right away (**Updated Forecast / `Posterior`**) and recommends the next step.

A **Pilot Scorecard Updater (Bayesian Network)** does the exact same thing for your AI investment.

---

## 2. The 6-Month Pilot Checkpoint Map

```text
[Leadership Support] & [Quality Guardrails]   (Layer 1: Company Foundation)
                 │
                 ▼
[6M Staff Usage] • [6M Cleanup Rate] • [6M Budget Control]   (Layer 2: 6-Month Pilot Scorecard)
                 │
                 ▼
      [Time-to-Profit Conversion]             (Layer 3: Turning Saved Hours into Value)
                 │
                 ▼
   [Updated 3-Year Return & Funding Call]     (Layer 4: Green Light / Fix First / Hold)
```

---

## 3. How 6-Month Pilot Results Change Your Funding Call

| 6-Month Pilot Scorecard | Staff Usage | Cleanup Rate | Budget Control | Updated 3-Year Return | Board Stage-Gate Call |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Great 6-Month Pilot** | High (`>75%`) | Clean (`<5%`) | On Budget | **`+170%` to `+200%`** | **GREEN LIGHT** (Release Next-Stage Funding) |
| **Average 6-Month Pilot** | On Target (`45–75%`) | Moderate (`5–10%`) | On Budget | **`+65%` to `+115%`** | **FIX FIRST** (Tighten Quality Before Scaling) |
| **Busy But Messy Pilot** | High (`>75%`) | Heavy (`>10%`) | Over Budget | **`+15%` to `+45%`** | **FIX FIRST / HOLD** (Stop Bill Creep & Rework) |
| **Struggling Pilot** | Low (`<45%`) | Heavy (`>10%`) | Over Budget | **`-10%` to `+10%`** | **HOLD / PAUSE** (Freeze New Seats & Redesign) |

---

## 4. From 6-Month Pilot to Board Funding Call (Visual Map)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    F["Leadership Support & Quality Guardrails"] --> P1["6M Staff Usage"]
    F --> P2["6M Cleanup Rate"]
    F --> P3["6M Budget Control"]
    P1 --> R["Time-to-Profit Conversion"]
    P2 --> R
    P3 --> R
    R --> G["Board Decision: Green Light / Fix First / Hold"]
    style F fill:#7c3aed,stroke:#6d28d9,color:#ffffff
    style P1 fill:#2563eb,stroke:#1d4ed8,color:#ffffff
    style P2 fill:#0284c7,stroke:#0369a1,color:#ffffff
    style P3 fill:#d97706,stroke:#b45309,color:#ffffff
    style R fill:#0d9488,stroke:#0f766e,color:#ffffff
    style G fill:#059669,stroke:#047857,color:#ffffff
```

---

## 5. How Stage-Gate Funding Protects Company Capital

The biggest financial mistake in enterprise technology is committing a full 3-year budget before testing whether teams actually use the tool. A **Pilot Scorecard Updater** gives the Board a clear, disciplined alternative: fund a focused **6-month pilot** first, then let real numbers—not vendor promises—decide what happens next.

If staff usage is high, cleanup is low, and usage bills stay on budget, you get an objective **Green Light** to scale company-wide. If cleanup or bills are creeping up, you get an early **Fix First** warning while the financial commitment is still small.

- **Source File:** [`BayesianNetworkModel.jl`](src/simulations/bayesian-network/BayesianNetworkModel.jl)
